correctness.rationale: Two landmark-free arms create equal distance vectors at equal depth, so every resolving set meets at least q-1 arms. A size-(q-1) resolving set is therefore one noncentral landmark on each of q-1 arms. For k<=L, its omitted leaf lies at distance at least L+1 and prevents distance-k domination. For ceil(L/2)<=k<L, choosing depth L-k on every arm dominates each arm end-to-end; for k=L, depth one on every arm works. For k>=L+1, depth-one landmarks on q-1 arms give a metric basis and dominate the omitted leaf. In the stabilized regime the omitted leaf has distance L+min d_i, which gives the exact optimizer criterion and counting formula. Exhaustive distance-vector and domination tests corroborate the theorem on 84 parameter-radius cases.

value.rationale: Balanced spiders are canonical one-branching-vertex trees. The theorem identifies the exact radius at which a combined domination/resolution parameter reaches the metric-dimension lower bound, cutting the general diameter guarantee from 2L to the sharp L+1 threshold. It also gives a nontrivial one-extra-landmark plateau and an exact classification and enumeration of every optimum after stabilization, so the result explains the structural mechanism rather than reporting a single value.
